paragraphs.source_en: Tokugawa Ieyasu believed that he had succeeded in making Masamune abandon his rebellious ambitions. Masamune was not a man like Ishida Mitsunari, who did not know when to advance and when to retreat. Ishida Mitsunari was certainly no fool; he knew perfectly well what the realm would become after Hideyoshi's death. Yet he was the kind of man who wished only to sacrifice himself for loyalty and honor. Unable to master himself, he went against the tide and brought defeat and ruin upon his own head.

units.source_zh: 德川家康相信自己已成功地令政宗收起了叛心。

paragraphs.source_en: Date Masamune, however, was not like that; he was capable of cool reflection. Mitsunari knew neither how to preserve himself through prudence nor how to conceal his talents and bide his time, whereas Masamune could adapt to circumstances. When he saw Ieyasu travel personally to Edo and carefully inspect the defenses around the city, he knew that all was lost.

paragraphs.source_en: The news from Europe for which Masamune had waited so desperately vanished without a trace. Katakura Kagetsuna, his right-hand man who had shared all his hardships and joys since youth, had also died of illness. His son-in-law Matsudaira Tadateru, whom he could use as a shield and even manipulate as a hostage, had been swiftly confined by Ieyasu in Fukaya Castle. Masamune's claws and fangs had, so to speak, all been broken.

Doi Toshikatsu, however, was displeased that Ieyasu neither punished Masamune nor abandoned the plan to marry the shogun's daughter to Masamune's son; he considered it an excessively ingratiating display of weakness.

paragraphs.source_en: It was at New Year that rumors of the Date raising an army once again spread wildly through the streets of Edo. “Perhaps he means to use the New Year festivities to catch us unawares.” Many among the shogun's close retainers agreed with this view. paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu welcomed the New Year of Genna 2 with Yorinobu and Yorifusa. paragraphs.source_en: In the Tanaka district east of Fujieda post station stood a small castle, built years before on Takeda Shingen's orders. Lord Shingen and Baba Mino-no-kami had both stayed there briefly. After the Takeda clan's downfall, Ieyasu enfeoffed his retainer Kori Kiyonaga there. Soon afterward, however, the Tokugawa were transferred to the Kanto, and Sunpu later became the domain of Nakamura Kazuuji. After the Battle of Sekigahara, the Nakamura clan was also transferred elsewhere, and the place became a guard castle for Sunpu.
